title: You Can't Drag Your Money Into The Grave With You [Postcard]

description.main: A Fotofolio postcard of Barbara Kruger's Untitled (You can't drag your money into the grave with you), a 1988 paste-up that sets a slogan about money and death over a photograph of new leather shoes on grass.
description.extended:
A Fotofolio postcard of Barbara Kruger's Untitled (You can't drag your money into the grave with you), a 1988 paste-up that sets a slogan about money and death over a photograph of new leather shoes on grass.

The card reproduces the image in color at 11 by 15 cm. Three white bands cross the black-and-white photograph. Each carries part of the sentence in Kruger's white-on-red Futura Bold Oblique, so the phrase assembles itself as the eye moves down the picture. The source work is photograph and type on paper, 18 by 23 cm, now in the Pinault Collection. A 1990 screen print on vinyl enlarged the image to nearly three by four metres. Fotofolio, a New York postcard publisher founded in 1975, issues several of Kruger's images as cards.

Kruger, born in Newark in 1945, worked as a magazine designer before turning in the late 1970s to found photographs captioned with declarative text. This card sits with late-1980s works on money such as To Buy or Not to Buy and Bleed Us Dry.
description.artist_bio: Barbara Kruger (b. 1945, Newark) is an American conceptual artist associated with the Pictures Generation. After working as a designer and picture editor at Conde Nast magazines, she began in the late 1970s to pair found black-and-white photographs with declarative text in Futura Bold Oblique, white on red. The Barbara Kruger Catalogue Raisonne (barbarakruger.org) documents the work; she is represented by Sprueth Magers and David Zwirner.

notes: Acquired from Printed Matter, New York: https://www.printedmatter.org/catalog/58684. Not signed. Printed Matter stock 120603 C. Fotofolio postcard, color, 11 x 15 cm, reproducing Kruger's Untitled (You can't drag your money into the grave with you), 1988, photograph and type on paper, 18 x 23 cm, Pinault Collection; a 1990 screen print on vinyl of the same image exists. The Printed Matter record is undated and the year of the Fotofolio printing could not be established, so year is left blank. No ISBN.
